sentences.text: The incident is said to have taken place on 14.8.2018 and at that time, the victim/prosecutrix was less than 17 years of age, therefore, the learned Trial Court has committed a blatant error in recording a finding of acquittal in favour of the respondent/accused overlooking the evidence as contained in her compliant (Exhibit P/1) so also her statement (Exhibit P/5) recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C.
As the victim/prosecutrix was minor at the time of the incident, therefore, the finding of acquittal recorded in favour of the respondent/accused by the learned Trial Court needs to be reversed.
3 We have heard learned Government Advocate for the appellant/State and gone through the record.

4 Exhibit P/3 is the MLC of the victim/prosecutrix, which was carried out on 29.9.2018 at 2:45AM wherein it is mentioned that the victim/prosecutrix narrated the sexual assault by her friend twice on 14.8.2018.
The girl was conscious oriented to time, place & period.
Her pulse was 88.
Her Blood Pressure was 110/70 MM Per HG.
On internal examination, no injury was seen over her private parts.
Her hymen old torn healed.

As the victim//prosecutrix was undergoing menstrual cycle,
therefore, the blood was oozing out.
PW.6 Dr.Yasmeen Niazi had referred the victim/prosecutrix to Radiologist but there is no Radiological Report available on record.

As per NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:36808 3 CRA-305-2023 the charge and the assertion of the victim/prosecutrix as contained in Exhibit P/1, her privacy was violated on 14.8.2018 and the respondent/accused had blackmailed her in the name of making her nude photographs viral and had taken her to his house behind Vikram School BHEL Quarter and had forcefully established the relationship with her.
5 The victim/prosecutrix (PW1) in Paragraph No.17 of her testimony admits that she had visited the house of the respondent/accused on several occasions.
He used to forcefully call her.
Her brother also used to visit the house of the respondent/accused.
Her brother came to know of their relationship after one year.
Her brother had not informed anything to her parents.
She admits that on 14.8.2018, her brother had also visited the house of the respondent/accused.

Thereafter, she on her own states that after twenty minutes of she leaving for the house of the respondent/accused, her brother had come and thereafter she had returned back with her brother to her own house.
Her brother did not inform her parents that the victim/prosecutrix had visited the house of the respondent/accused.
The victim/prosecutrix admits that her mother had knowledge of she being outside her house at night.
Her mother had scolded her but since her brother was with her, she informed her mother that they got late and she was with her brother.

The victim/prosecutrix in Paragraph No.21 of her testimony admits that on 26.9.2018, the respondent/accused had called her mother and had informed her that the victim/prosecutrix was troubling her for last two years.

She admits that the respondent/accused had not sent any of the nude photographs to her father &
mother.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:36808 4 CRA-305-2023 6 PW.7

Krishna Pratap Singh,
Sub Inspector of Police Station Piplani, District Bhopal states that he had prepared the Spot Map (Exhibit P/4) at the instance of the victim/prosecutrix.
On 30.9.2018, he had conducted the search in the house of the respondent/accused alongwith witnesses Gyarasi & Ghanshyam.
He had not found any Pen Drive, Laptop etc nor any Photograph was recovered vide Exhibit P/10.

He had The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Prashant Singh on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80760289/
2 seized a Samsung Galaxy J7 Mobile with 2 Sims of Jio & Idea Company from the possession of the respondent/accused.

sentences.text: There were several photographs of the respondent/accused with the victim/prosecutrix in the gallery of the mobile but it is nowhere stated by the Investigating Officer that any of the photographs of the victim/prosecutrix or the respondent/accused were in a compromising position or were exposing the privacy of the victim/prosecutrix.
7 PW.7
Krishna Pratap Singh admits that the complaint was given on 28.9.2018 narrating the incident, which is said to have taken place on 14.8.2018.
Thus, there was delay of about one and a half months in reporting the matter.
No reason was given for such delay.
He admits that no independent witness was confronted to prove that on the time and date of the incident, the victim/prosecutrix was not in her house.
He also admits that there was no independent witness to prove that at the time and date of the incident, the victim/prosecutrix was in the house of the respondent/accused.

He admits that he could not collect any physical evidence like call details etc to prove that either on the date of the incident or after lodging of the report, the respondent/accused was in contact with the victim/prosecutrix and had NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:36808 5 CRA-305-2023 met her somewhere.
While preparing the Spot Map, he could not lay hands on any physical evidence.

This witness has denied a suggestion that since the cousin sister of the victim/prosecutrix and her father were indulging in the act of forceful conversion and the respondent/accused Prashant Singh, Aman & Vishal had refused to come under pressure

,
therefore, a false case has been prepared.

8 PW.7 Krishna Pratap Singh in Paragraph No.20 of his testimony clearly states that the mobile of the respondent/accused contains several photographs but there was no nude photograph and no photograph of the victim/prosecutrix with the respondent/accused was found in any compromising position.
There was no such material, which can be said to be the cause of blackmailing the victim/prosecutrix and may force her to establish physical relationship with the respondent/accused against her will.

9 Thus, it is evident that there is a suggestion to the victim/prosecutrix that there was an attempt to convert the respondent/accused Prashant Singh and when that attempt failed and Prashant Singh reported the matter to the mother of the victim/prosecutrix of being harassed by the victim/prosecutrix, the FIR came to be lodged against the respondent/accused.
The respondent/accused in his statement recorded under Section 313 of the Cr.P.C clearly states that the Missionary and other Christian persons were forcing him to convert and
since he refused to convert,
a false case has been registered against him.

10 When all these aspects are taken into consideration then it is evident that the learned Trial Court h a s m i n u t e l y s c r u t i n i z e d t h e e v i d e n c e f o r w h i c h N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .

it needs a word of appreciation and after minutely scrutinizing the evidence and without getting swayed with the emotional aspect of the testimony of the victim/prosecutrix and the other prosecution witnesses, the learned Trial Court has been able to separate the grains from chaff and when the impugned judgment dated 18.8.2022 passed by learned XIII Additional Sessions Judge- Special Judge (POCSO Act) in Special Case No.433/2021 is tested in this backdrop then it does not does not call for any interference in the light of the judgment of the Apex Court in Chandrappa & Others versus State of Karnataka (2007) 4 SCC 415, which says that if two views are possible on the basis of the evidence on record and one favourable to the accused has The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Prashant Singh on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80760289/
3 been taken by the learned Trial Court then it ought not to be disturbed by the Appellate Court.

sentences.text: More over, as the prosecution could not prove its case beyond reasonable doubt, therefore, the aspect of the age of the victim/prosecutrix becomes immaterial and in absence of the sexual assault being proved merely on the basis of the fact that the victim/prosecutrix was minor at that time, is not sufficient to uphold the conviction of the respondent/accused especially when there is no DNA or FSL report available on record.
11 Resultantly, the appeal filed by the appellant/State is dismissed.
12 Let record of the Trial Court be sent back.
